Winter shutoff protection: Oct 1, 2026 – Apr 30, 2027 (Cold Weather Rule). A utility may not disconnect, and must reconnect, heat for qualifying customers who set up and keep a payment plan.
Who is covered: Residential heating customers. The utility may not disconnect, and must reconnect, heat for households at or below 50% of state median income that set up and keep a payment plan.
Temperature rule: None found in the cited rule (date-based)
Heating help (LIHEAP): Check availability. Commerce lists the 2026–27 deadline as May 31, 2027.

Winter shutoff protection: Oct 12, 2026 – Apr 16, 2027 (Special Reconnect Order). Pay up to $175, plus a reconnection fee of up to $36, to keep or restore electric or gas service, even if you owe more. You can use it once per winter heating season.
Who is covered: Not a shutoff ban. Any residential customer of a PUCO-regulated gas or electric utility can pay up to $175, plus up to $36 to reconnect, to keep or restore service once this winter. No income limit.
Temperature rule: None found in the cited rule (date-based)
Heating help (LIHEAP): Check availability. The state's HEAP page says applications are accepted July 1, 2026 – May 31, 2027.

Winter shutoff protection: Nov 1, 2026 – Mar 31, 2027 (Winter Protection Plan). Customers must keep up the plan's payments. Customers 65 or older also have shutoff protection for the same dates.
Who is covered: Customers 65 or older. Income-qualified customers (at or below 150% of the federal poverty level, or getting MDHHS cash assistance, SSI, SNAP or Medicaid) on the Winter Protection Plan who keep up its payments.
Temperature rule: None final. Each utility has its own extreme-weather policy; the MPSC is reviewing them in Case U-20140

Winter shutoff protection: Nov 1, 2026 to Apr 15, 2027. Utilities can't shut off heat to an occupied home at or below 250% of the federal poverty level, or where someone's health would be endangered. Above that, a shutoff is a last resort under procedures the PSC must approve.
Who is covered: Occupied homes where the utility service is, or runs, the main heat. A shutoff is allowed only for households above 250% of the federal poverty level where no one's health or safety would be endangered.
Temperature rule: None found in the cited rule (date-based)
Rule source: Wis. Admin. Code PSC 113.0304; PSC of Wisconsin

Winter shutoff protection: Nov 1, 2026 – Apr 15, 2027 (cold weather period). Before shutting off heat-related service, utilities must try to reach the household and check for serious harm to health or safety. If harm is likely, the shutoff waits at least 15 business days while social services is notified.
Who is covered: Not a shutoff ban. For residential heat-related gas, electric or steam service, the utility must try to reach the household and check for serious harm to health or safety. If harm is likely, the shutoff waits at least 15 business days while social services is notified.
Temperature rule: None found in the cited rule (date-based)
Heating help (LIHEAP): Regular HEAP opens Nov 2, 2026 (Governor's office, Oct 16, 2026). Emergency HEAP opens Jan 4, 2027.

Winter shutoff protection: Nov 1, 2026 – Apr 1, 2027. Utilities may not disconnect households certified eligible for LIHEAP or weatherization. Not a ban on all shutoffs. The bill is still owed.
Who is covered: Households certified eligible for LIHEAP or weatherization; the bill is still owed. Separately, gas heat can't be shut off when the temperature or 24-hour forecast is 20°F or colder.
Temperature rule: Gas or electric heat that is the only heat source can't be shut off when the temperature, or the National Weather Service 24-hour forecast, is 20°F or colder (Iowa Admin. Code 199-19.4)
Heating help (LIHEAP): General applications open Nov 1, 2026. Early applications opened Oct 1, 2026 for households with a resident age 60 or older or a disabled resident. Applications are accepted through Apr 30, 2027 (checked Oct 27, 2026).

Winter shutoff protection: Nov 15, 2026 – Mar 15, 2027 (Winter Termination Program). Covered customers' gas, electric, water and wastewater service can't be shut off.
Who is covered: Customers getting Lifeline, HEAP, TANF, SSI, PAAD, General Assistance or USF, water-assistance applicants, and others the BPU lists. Covers gas, electric, water and wastewater.
Temperature rule: None found in the cited rule (date-based)

Winter shutoff protection: Nov 15, 2026 – Mar 15, 2027 in state law. Gas or electric companies may not shut off heating service to a customer who can't pay because of financial hardship. This winter the DPU says it requested to expand the moratorium to Nov 1, 2026 – Apr 1, 2027 (Mass.gov DPU, checked Oct 22, 2026); ask your utility which dates it is using.
Who is covered: Residential customers who use gas or electric service for heat and can't pay because of financial hardship. Ask your utility which dates it is using.
Temperature rule: None found in the cited rule (date-based)
Heating help (LIHEAP): HEAP covers heating costs Nov 1, 2026 – Apr 30, 2027. New middle-income heating oil benefit (up to $680) opens in December 2026.
Notes: Starts and Ends are the dates in state law (M.G.L. c. 164, § 124F). The DPU says it requested Nov 1, 2026 to Apr 1, 2027 for this winter (Mass.gov DPU, checked Oct 22, 2026); ask your utility which dates it uses.

Winter shutoff protection: Dec 1, 2026 – Mar 31, 2027. Gas or electric utilities can't disconnect a home heated by gas or electricity for nonpayment unless they first offered a deferred payment plan and the customer refused it. No disconnection at all for Energy Assistance Act participants or customers who told the utility they are a service member or veteran.
Who is covered: Homes heated by gas or electricity: no shutoff unless the utility offered a deferred payment plan and the customer refused it. No shutoff at all for Energy Assistance Act participants or customers who told the utility they are a service member or veteran. Separately, no heat shutoff on days forecast at 32°F or below.
Temperature rule: No shutoff of gas or electric heat on a day when the National Weather Service forecast for the next 24 hours is 32°F or below (220 ILCS 5/8-205; 83 Ill. Adm. Code 280.130(n))

Winter shutoff protection: Dec 1, 2026 – Mar 31, 2027. Electric and gas utilities may not terminate service for qualifying households unless the PUC allows it.
Who is covered: Electric and gas customers with household income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level, unless the PUC allows a shutoff.
Temperature rule: None found in the cited rule (date-based)
Heating help (LIHEAP): Check availability. The state says the 2026–27 LIHEAP season is scheduled to open Nov 2, 2026.

Winter shutoff protection: Dec 1, 2026 – Mar 15, 2027. Electric and gas utilities may not disconnect customers who are eligible for and have applied for energy assistance (EAP). Not a ban on all shutoffs.
Who is covered: Not a ban on all shutoffs. Electric and gas customers receiving energy assistance (EAP), or qualified for it, who have applied and given the utility written proof.
Temperature rule: None found in the cited rule (date-based)
Heating help (LIHEAP): State page lists the EAP application window as Oct 1, 2026 – Apr 30, 2027. Check availability.
